name: Determine high-performing data ingestion and transformation solutions

lesson.summary: Choose the ingestion path by data shape and latency: streams (Kinesis Data Streams, MSK), managed delivery (Amazon Data Firehose), file transfer (DataSync, Transfer Family), and then transform and query with Glue and Athena.
keyPoints: Kinesis Data Streams ingests real-time data, keeps records for a retention period, and supports multiple independent consumers
Amazon Data Firehose delivers streaming data to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch and other destinations with no consumer code
DataSync transfers data online between on-premises storage such as NFS or SMB and AWS storage, and tasks can run on a schedule
AWS Snowball Edge is no longer available to new customers; for new transfers use DataSync for online transfers or AWS Data Transfer Terminal for physical transfers
Glue is serverless ETL with a Data Catalog; Athena queries S3 with SQL

scenarios.text: A retail company collects point-of-sale events from 2,000 stores. Events must be processed within seconds by a fraud-detection application, and the same events must also be stored in Amazon S3 as columnar files so analysts can query them with Amazon Athena. The team is small and wants the least operational overhead and no servers to manage.

questions.prompt: An application must ingest real-time clickstream data, let several independent consumers process it, and be able to replay recent records. Which service fits?

options.text: Amazon SQS standard queue
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration
AWS DataSync

questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams keeps records for a retention period and allows multiple applications to consume the same stream independently, so records can be re-read. An SQS consumer deletes each message after processing and SQS typically serves a single subscriber, so it does not give replay to several consumers. Transfer Acceleration speeds object uploads, and DataSync copies files between storage systems rather than ingesting streaming records.

questions.prompt: A team wants streaming log data delivered to Amazon S3 in compressed batches with no custom consumer code and minimal operations. Which service should they use?

options.text: Amazon MSK with a self-written consumer on EC2
AWS Glue crawlers
Amazon Data Firehose
Amazon EMR long-running cluster

questions.explanation: Amazon Data Firehose is a fully managed service that buffers streaming data, can transform it before delivery, and delivers it to S3 with optional compression, with no applications to write. MSK plus EC2 and EMR need infrastructure and code, and Glue crawlers catalog data rather than ingest streams.

questions.prompt: A company must copy a 200 TB archive from an on-premises NFS NAS to Amazon S3 over its fast network link and then keep S3 in sync with the NAS every night. Which TWO actions meet the requirement with the least custom code?

options.text: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the NAS data to S3 online
Amazon Data Firehose for the 200 TB archive
Run the DataSync task on a nightly schedule
AWS Glue crawlers for the nightly sync
Amazon CloudFront for the initial 200 TB

questions.explanation: DataSync works with on-premises NFS storage and transfers data to S3 over the network, and a DataSync task can run on a schedule with cron or rate expressions, so a nightly run keeps S3 in sync. Data Firehose delivers streaming records, Glue crawlers catalog data rather than copy it, and CloudFront delivers content to users rather than ingesting it.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to query raw CSV files in S3 with SQL without managing servers.
steps: Query the table with Amazon Athena
Run an AWS Glue crawler to populate the Data Catalog
Land the CSV files in an S3 bucket
questions.explanation: Data must first exist in S3, then a Glue crawler infers the schema into the Data Catalog, and finally Athena queries the cataloged table.

questions.prompt: Match each requirement to the service.

pairs.left: Serverless ETL jobs and a Data Catalog
Serverless SQL queries directly on S3 data
Partners uploading files over SFTP into S3

questions.explanation: Each pairing reflects the service's purpose: Glue for ETL, Athena for interactive SQL on S3, MSK for Kafka, and Transfer Family for managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP into AWS storage.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service provides serverless ETL with a central Data Catalog and can run Apache Spark jobs?
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service that includes the Data Catalog, crawlers and Spark-based ETL jobs.

questions.prompt: A Kinesis data stream has two consumers that each call GetRecords. Both are slowed down because they share the 2 MB per second per-shard read throughput. What change gives each consumer its own dedicated read throughput with the lowest latency?

options.text: Add a second stream and write every record twice
Register the consumers as enhanced fan-out consumers
Increase the stream retention period to 7 days
Replace the stream with an SQS standard queue

questions.explanation: Enhanced fan-out gives each registered consumer its own dedicated throughput per shard, pushed over HTTP/2, so consumers no longer compete. Writing twice doubles producer work and cost without addressing the cause. A longer retention period changes how long records are kept, not read throughput. An SQS queue removes the replay and multiple-consumer model.

questions.prompt: A company streams JSON events into Amazon Data Firehose and delivers them to S3. Athena queries on this data are slow and expensive. What is the simplest way to improve query performance and cost?

options.text: Enable record format conversion in Firehose to write Apache Parquet files
Add a Lambda function that gzips each record individually
Switch the destination to Amazon RDS
Increase the Firehose buffer size to the maximum for JSON

questions.explanation: Firehose can convert JSON records to Parquet or ORC before delivery, and columnar formats let Athena scan far less data. Gzipping single records does not create a columnar layout. RDS is not an analytics store for this volume and adds operations. A larger buffer creates bigger files but they remain row-based JSON that Athena must scan in full.

questions.prompt: Business partners must upload files to Amazon S3 using their existing SFTP clients. The company wants to avoid running and patching SFTP servers. Which service meets this requirement?

options.text: Amazon EC2 instances running an open-source SFTP daemon
AWS DataSync agent in each partner network
AWS Transfer Family with an SFTP server endpoint
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams

questions.explanation: AWS Transfer Family provides a managed SFTP endpoint that stores files directly in S3, so partners keep their clients and there are no servers to manage. EC2 with an SFTP daemon works but requires patching and scaling. DataSync is for bulk transfers from storage you control, not partner client uploads. Kinesis ingests streaming records, not files over SFTP.

questions.prompt: A nightly AWS Glue ETL job reads an S3 prefix that receives new files every day. Each run currently reprocesses all historical files. Which feature makes the job process only new data?

options.text: Glue Data Catalog table versioning
Increasing the number of DPUs
Glue crawler scheduling every hour
Glue job bookmarks

questions.explanation: Job bookmarks let a Glue job track data it has already processed and handle only new data on later runs. Table versioning records schema changes, not processed files. More DPUs speed up the same full scan but still reprocess everything. Crawlers update catalog metadata and do not control which data the job reads.

questions.prompt: A Kinesis data stream with provisioned shards shows throttled writes on one shard while others are idle. All records use the same partition key, the device type. What is the best fix?

options.text: Use a partition key with higher cardinality, such as a device ID, so records spread across shards
Reduce the retention period to 24 hours
Switch the producers to the GetRecords API
Add an SQS queue in front of the stream to absorb the load

questions.explanation: Records with the same partition key go to the same shard, so a low-cardinality key creates a hot shard; a high-cardinality key spreads writes evenly. Retention does not affect write throughput. GetRecords is a consumer API, not a producer one. An SQS queue adds a component and does not fix the uneven key distribution.

questions.prompt: A company needs to compute rolling 1-minute aggregates on data in a Kinesis data stream and write the results to another stream, using SQL or Apache Flink code but without managing a cluster. Which service fits?

options.text: AWS Glue crawler
Amazon Athena
Amazon EMR on a self-managed EC2 fleet
Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink

questions.explanation: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink runs continuous stream processing, including windowed aggregations, on managed infrastructure and can read from and write to Kinesis streams. A Glue crawler only infers schemas. Athena runs interactive queries on data at rest in S3, not continuous windows on a stream. EMR on self-managed EC2 works but requires cluster management.

questions.prompt: Athena queries filter by date on a large table in S3, but each query scans all objects. Which change reduces the data scanned the most with the least effort?

options.text: Rename the objects with a date suffix
Partition the data by date in the S3 key layout and register the partitions
Move the data to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval
Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration

questions.explanation: Partitioning by date lets Athena prune partitions and read only the matching prefixes. A date suffix in object names is not a partition, so Athena still lists and scans everything. Glacier Flexible Retrieval objects cannot be queried directly and do not reduce scans. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads over long distances and has no effect on query scanning.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about Amazon Data Firehose are correct?

options.text: It can deliver streaming data to Amazon S3 and Amazon OpenSearch Service
It requires you to provision and manage shards
It stores records for replay by multiple independent consumers
It can invoke a Lambda function to transform records before delivery
It can only deliver data to Amazon Redshift

questions.explanation: Firehose delivers to destinations such as S3 and OpenSearch Service and can use Lambda to transform records in flight. It has no shards to manage, which is a Kinesis Data Streams concept. It does not offer replay to multiple consumers; that is Data Streams. Redshift is one destination among several, not the only one.

questions.prompt: A company must move 30 TB of data from an on-premises SMB file server to Amazon S3 over a 1 Gbps link and verify the data arrived intact, with minimal scripting. Which TWO choices help?

options.text: Deploy a DataSync agent on premises and create a task from the SMB location to S3
Use Amazon Data Firehose with a custom producer for each file
Enable DataSync data integrity verification on the task
Use Glue crawlers to copy the files to S3
Mount the SMB share on Amazon CloudFront

questions.explanation: A DataSync agent can read from an SMB location and the task copies to S3, and DataSync can verify the transferred data against the source. Firehose is for streaming records, so building file transfers on it needs custom code. Glue crawlers catalog data and do not copy it. CloudFront is a content delivery network and cannot mount a file share.

questions.prompt: Which solution meets the requirements with the least operational overhead?

options.text: Send events to a Kinesis data stream; process them with a Lambda function for fraud detection and use Amazon Data Firehose with Parquet conversion to deliver the same stream to S3
Write events directly to S3 and run AWS Glue crawlers every minute for fraud detection
Send events to an SQS standard queue and have two consumers read the same messages
Run Apache Kafka on EC2 instances with a custom S3 sink application

questions.explanation: Kinesis Data Streams ingests the events in real time, Lambda can react within seconds, and Firehose can read from the stream and write Parquet to S3 for Athena, all without servers. Crawlers on S3 data are batch cataloging, not seconds-level processing. An SQS message is removed once one consumer handles it, so two consumers cannot both read it. Kafka on EC2 and a custom sink need cluster and code management.

questions.prompt: Put the steps in order to deliver streaming application logs to S3 with Amazon Data Firehose.
steps: Verify the delivered objects in the S3 bucket
Send records to the delivery stream with the PutRecord API
Create a Firehose delivery stream that targets the bucket
questions.explanation: The bucket must exist before a delivery stream can target it, the stream must exist before producers send records, and objects can be checked in S3 after Firehose buffers and delivers them.
